messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts on Dedicated cluster gpu-42 affecting tenant 'FariaTech'. Auto-page to oncall. first_seen=2026-03-15T18:02:14Z metrics: 5xx_rate=12% (baseline 0.4%), p95 latency 2.4s.

Anna (oncall): ack. I'm looking. Paging SRE/infra. Maria, any customer alerts?

Maria (CSM): FariaTech is starting to report errors on their dashboards. They called support and flagged a spike in failed generations since ~18:00 UTC. No data exfil concerns — just availability.

Jay (eng-runtime): pulling runtime logs now. Seeing a lot of 502 from gateway -> model-hosts and repeated 'kv cache miss' bursts. Example from gateway logs:```
[18:02:10] gateway - request_id=abc123 - upstream_error=EOF
[18:02:11] gateway - request_id=abc124 - upstream_error=timeout
[18:02:12] runtime - model_host=10.23.5.9 - kv_evictions=112 - free_mem=2%
```

Lee (infra): checking cluster metrics. GPU util on pool gpu-42 is pegged at 98% on a subset of nodes. Network egress and socket queues are backed up. Also seeing OOM kills on a worker pod and kubelet eviction events. Looks like noisy tenant is saturating a few nodes.

Tim (ops): can we triage to noisy neighbor vs genuine model bug? Any recent deploys?

Jay (eng-runtime): no deploys to that model in the last 3 hours. Pattern: single tenant FariaTech traffic shows bursty long-seq requests. Continuous batching + long seq -> KV pressure -> evictions -> upstream timeouts -> 502s. Likely capacity exhaustion/noisy neighbor.

Anna (oncall): mitigation plan options: (1) throttle tenant at edge, (2) evict heavy pods from affected nodes and cordon, (3) bump dedicated pool size / scale up, (4) fallback routing to compatible smaller model variant. Which we can do fastest?

Lee (infra): fastest is throttle at LB and fallback routing. We can also add two spare nodes but that takes ~5-7 minutes to warm up. Evicting pods and cordoning is immediate but causes some disruption.

Tim (ops): I'll apply a soft throttle rule on tenant traffic to 30rps for now. Command:```
# update rate-limit rule for tenant fariatech
redwoodctl routing update-rate --tenant fariatech --limit 30
```
Applying...

Tim (ops): done. rate-limit applied. Observing immediate drop in queue length at gateway. 5xx rate down to ~7% (from 12%).

Jay (eng-runtime): pushing a compatible smaller model fallback as a safety net. Will update routing policy to prefer model-v2-quant when latency SLO satisfied.```
# add fallback policy
redwoodctl routing add-fallback --tenant fariatech --from model-v3-large --to model-v2-quant --threshold 4% --window 60s
```
Policy added.

Maria (CSM): told FariaTech we are actively mitigating, they appreciate the quick response. Asking for ETA to normal operations.

Anna (oncall): status check after throttling + fallback: Jay, Lee, sync on pod evictions and node saturation?

Lee (infra): evicted two heavy pods from nodes node-7 and node-8, cordoned node-7 pending investigation. Kubelet logs show kernel OOM on node-8 causing pod restarts. GPU memory fragmentation high. I'm scheduling a drain on node-8 for deeper analysis.

Jay (eng-runtime): logs post-throttle: upstream timeouts reduced significantly. KV eviction rate down 80%. p95 latency trending toward baseline. Still seeing occasional 502 spikes when client long-seq bursts sneak through.

Anna (oncall): good. Next: temporarily isolate FariaTech to a quieter pool if acceptable. Lee, can we shift their slot to a less-loaded pool?

Lee (infra): we can warm a warm pool 'gpu-43' and move tenant, but live migration will take ~3 minutes and some requests may fail during cutover. Recommend staged cutover with traffic drain.

Tim (ops): I'll coordinate cutover window, doing staged 10% increments via routing.```
# staged cutover
redwoodctl routing migrate-tenant --tenant fariatech --to-pool gpu-43 --stage 10,30,60,100 --interval 30s
```
Starting migration.

incident-bot: Automated note: oncall handoff detected upcoming at 22:00 UTC. Marking this incident for potential follow-up.

Jay (eng-runtime): migration at 30% shows error rate at 2.1%. p95 latency 520ms. Migration proceeding.

Maria (CSM): customer reports partial recovery on their side, dashboards improving. They're asking for a post-incident summary and whether this is likely to reoccur.

Anna (oncall): quick customer-facing note: we've throttled FariaTech heavy bursts and routed them to a fallback model while we evacuate saturated nodes. We're moving them to an isolated pool and monitoring. ETA ~15-20 minutes to full recovery.

Lee (infra): migration complete to gpu-43. Node saturation resolved. I'm uncordoning node-7 for investigation later. GPU memory fragmentation and a runaway batcher from that tenant caused the problem. We'll capture artifacts.

Jay (eng-runtime): marking mitigations: throttling, fallback routing, staged migration. Follow-ups: (a) throttle policy tuning per-tenant, (b) improve detection for KV eviction bursts, (c) autoscale warm pool faster, (d) add tenant-level burst protection in router.

Tim (ops): logging commands/artifacts:```
# collect runtime snapshots
redwoodctl diagnostics collect --cluster gpu-42 --since 18:00 --out /tmp/fariatech_incident.tar.gz
```
Snapshot collected and uploaded to s3://rdw-incidents/2356001234.tar.gz

Anna (oncall): handing off to Priya (oncall-night) at 22:00 UTC for overnight monitoring. Priya, TL;DR: FariaTech noisy-neighbor caused KV evictions and OOMs on gpu-42 -> throttled tenant, applied fallback routing, migrated to gpu-43. Recovery observed; 5xx back to baseline. Artifacts uploaded. Please watch for reoccurrence and start postmortem doc.

Priya (oncall-night): ack. I'll monitor p95 & 5xx and will start the postmortem doc in #incidents-postmortems. If we see any re-escalation I'll notify.

Maria (CSM): I'll draft a customer-facing blurb and coordinate with support.

Anna (oncall): closing active mitigation. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Setting follow-up label: postmortem-required, customer-communication.

incident-bot: Incident auto-update: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, linked_ticket=INC-235600.

Priya (oncall-night): one more note — please attach kernel logs and the evicted pod YAMLs to the postmortem. I'll pick this up at handoff.

Jay (eng-runtime): saved pod yamls and kernel logs to the snapshot tarball.

Anna (oncall): thanks team. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
